assessment.progress: Complete JSON lines are accepted only with exact keys, a fixed phase enum and contiguous integer sequences. Both bytes and text inputs are supported. Processing is capped at 64 KiB and 32 events.
assessment.partialData: Timeout/nonzero output contributes only the last validated phase and event count. Partial inventory/resource payload is not decoded or measured. Invalid or oversized progress is unobserved, not a resource measurement.
assessment.finalProtocol: Successful resource decoding still requires a complete validated final private payload. Any preceding lines must all be valid sequenced progress; malformed prefixes reject the reply.
assessment.privacy: Only fixed phase names/counts reach helperProgress. Raw output, partial payload, stderr, process identifiers, paths, arguments, environment and arbitrary exception text remain outside that projection.

limitations: A marker identifies the last observed execution point. It does not prove the following kernel call was entered or blocked; scheduling and termination may occur after the marker.
Unobserved progress may mean no complete output, invalid encoding/protocol or exceeded bounds. It does not uniquely identify interpreter startup/import failure.
Emitting phase evidence adds observation overhead and does not repair or prove the historical timeout cause.
The existing communicate timeout excludes process creation and kill/reap overhead; there is no strict 9.5-second wall-clock guarantee.
No full-build, checkpoint or native-authentication qualification follows from a short diagnostic result.
